concept_html:
Article 6 of the UK GDPR gives six lawful bases. Each use of personal data needs one that fits it:

  • consent
  • contract, to perform a contract with the person, such as paying their salary
  • legal obligation, such as tax reporting or right-to-work checks
  • vital interests, to protect someone's life
  • public task
  • legitimate interests

Since 5 February 2026, the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 adds recognised legitimate interests: a short, fixed list of purposes, such as safeguarding and crime prevention, that skip the balancing test. Commercial uses are not on it.

Employers rarely rely on consent. The ICO's view is that the power imbalance between employer and worker makes it hard for consent to be freely given. A worker who fears saying no has no genuine choice. Use another basis.

Workforce analytics usually rests on legitimate interests. The ICO describes a three-part test, recorded in a legitimate interests assessment (LIA) before processing starts:

  1. Purpose: is there a legitimate interest?
  2. Necessity: does the processing serve it, and is there a less intrusive way?
  3. Balancing: do the person's interests, rights and freedoms override yours? Ask what a reasonable person would expect.

Two principles from Article 5 shape the platform. Purpose limitation: a basis covers the purposes you specified. Payroll under contract does not cover an attrition model. A new purpose needs its own check. Data minimisation: hold only the data each purpose needs.

engagement_survey: {lawful_basis: legitimate_interests, lia: LIA-007}
attrition_model: {lawful_basis: legitimate_interests, lia: LIA-012, fields: minimised}

title: A lawful basis for each use of talent data
why_html: A firm launched an engagement survey and stated that consent was its lawful basis. Two years later it fed the answers into a promotion-readiness model. Staff complained that they had never agreed to that use, and some withdrew consent, which removed their records from every analysis. A legitimate interests assessment for each purpose, done before launch, would have shown that the promotion use failed the balancing test.
